headline: WSJ reports US intelligence concludes Putin ordered expanded covert sabotage campaign against NATO countries
dek: US intelligence agencies concluded Putin personally ordered a stepped-up sabotage/covert-action campaign against NATO countries; the failed August drone attack on an Antonov freighter at Leipzig-Halle Airport (Semtex-loaded drones, German mobile-network control) was an opening shot. Aides to…
sources: Wall Street Journal (original, gated: wsj.com/world/europe/airfield-attack-marked-opening-shot-in-putins-sabotage-campaign-against-europe-115dedd4), citing 'European officials briefed on US intelligence findings'
fault_line: Real Putin-ordered shadow war on NATO, or unproven intelligence used to lock Europe into confrontation (and cover the US diesel deal)? The evidence is classified; Russia denies.

sections.what_happened: US intelligence agencies concluded Putin personally ordered a stepped-up sabotage/covert-action campaign against NATO countries; the failed August drone attack on an Antonov freighter at Leipzig-Halle Airport (Semtex-loaded drones, German mobile-network control) was an opening shot. Aides to Chancellor Merz said Berlin would have considered invoking NATO Article 5 had casualties been heavy. Kremlin back-channel warned Berlin 'it won't be the last.' Attribution: GRU Special Tasks Service; logistics via Serbia (7 arrested). Russia denies involvement.
sections.what_verified: WSJ original + 5 relays converging on same details (Semtex drones, Article 5 contemplation, Serbia arrests, Oleg Levushkin/Belarusian operatives). Germany formally accused Russia of the Leipzig attempt on Sep 1 (established earlier). Telegraph/Welt investigation traced drones to GRU-linked intermediaries.
sections.what_disputed: Russia denies involvement in any sabotage in Europe. The WSJ's core claim (Putin personally ordered it) rests on unnamed European officials citing US intelligence — no public evidence presented; one relay notes the claims 'reflect intelligence findings relayed through unnamed sources, not publicly presented evidence.'
sections.why_matters: Present strictly as a US-INTELLIGENCE CLAIM (never fact): Washington's spies say Putin ordered it, Berlin weighed Article 5 — while Russia denies and no evidence is public. Contrast with the US waiving Russian energy sanctions the same month (diesel deal) — the West condemns sabotage while buying the oil.
sections.context: Background: NATO/Russia — NEW: WSJ reports US intelligence concludes Putin ordered expanded covert sabotage campaign against NATO countries; Leipzig drone attack was an 'opening shot'; Merz aides say Article 5 was considered

totw_analysis: Our read: Present strictly as a US-INTELLIGENCE CLAIM (never fact): Washington's spies say Putin ordered it, Berlin weighed Article 5 — while Russia denies and no evidence is public. Contrast with the US waiving Russian energy sanctions the same month (diesel deal) — the West condemns sabotage while buying the oil. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Real Putin-ordered shadow war on NATO, or unproven intelligence used to lock Europe into confrontation (and cover the US diesel deal)? The evidence is classified; Russia denies.
